title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down relative to the scan, and a long diagonal stroke runs across it. Read after a 180° rotation, it is a scratch verification of the standard identities of divided powers. The variable letters are hard to read, so the reading is plausible rather than certain.

(1) Product identity: x^{[i]} x^{[j]} = ((i+j)!/(i! j!)) x^{[i+j]}. The fraction i!j!/(i+j)!, inverted on the scan, is visible at the top left.

(2) The rules (ab)^{[n]} = a^n b^{[n]} and (a+b)^{[n]} = Σ_{i+j=n} a^{[i]} b^{[j]}. These appear as the chain of equalities on the left that expands products and sums with lower indices (n-i), (i).

(3) Composition identity: (x^{[i]})^{[j]} = ((ij)!/(j!(i!)^j)) x^{[ij]}. A fraction of this shape is legible upper right, with a computation of x^{[i]}-type terms indexed by (n-i), (i) underneath.

(4) A multi-index version (bottom of the rotated page): the conditions λ+μ=ν are written with vector arrows, and sums Σ_{λ+μ=ν} x^{[λ]} y^{[μ]} are factored as products of two sums. This is the identity exp(x+y) = exp(x)·exp(y) for divided-power exponential series, i.e. the generating-series form of the binomial rule for a polynomial algebra with divided powers in several variables.

Purpose: the neighbouring pages build categories M_N of graded modules over a graded algebra S, with truncation functors τ_N, quotient functors q_N, and adjoints ρ_N defined via Hom^i(τ_{N'-i}S, P). In this cote on the divided power de Rham complex, S is presumably the divided power polynomial algebra or its dual symmetric algebra. This page checks that the multiplication on the divided power algebra Γ(V) satisfies the PD axioms, or equivalently that the coproduct and multiplication are compatible.
errors: The page is too fragmentary and crossed out to verify every line. The legible identities are the standard correct ones; no evident error. The diagonal stroke may mean Grothendieck discarded the page or considered it done.

ideas.what: Axioms and identities for divided powers: binomial rule, product rule x^{[i]}x^{[j]} = binom(i+j,i) x^{[i+j]}, and the composition rule γ_j(γ_i(x)) = (ij)!/(j!(i!)^j) γ_{ij}(x)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (1954-55 seminar), N. Roby (1963-65); in crystalline cohomology Grothendieck/Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1966 letter to Tate and the 1968 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés) use PD-structures; systematic treatment in Berthelot's thesis

ideas.what: Multi-index divided power polynomial algebra and the factorisation Σ_{λ+μ=ν} x^{[λ]}y^{[μ]} as an exponential-type product of series
ideas.modern_name: Divided power polynomial algebra Γ(V) / PD-exponential, Hopf algebra structure

deep.surprise_reason: A routine scratch verification of standard divided-power identities, upside down and crossed out. It supports the module-category constructions on the neighbouring pages but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page must be rotated 180° to read. The fraction read as (i+j)!/(i!j!) is correct in rotated orientation.
The fragment read as (ix)!/(i!(x!)^i) is plausibly the composition constant (ij)!/(i!(j!)^i) or (pq)!/(p!(q!)^p) for (x^{[q]})^{[p]}.
Indices transcribed '(1-x)' and '(x)' are likely '(n-i)' and '(i)' read upside down.
The symbols transcribed 'Z' are likely summation signs Σ, or ν, read upside down.
Bottom right of the scan (top of the rotated page) has 'λ+μ=ν' with vector arrows over the letters (multi-indices), not plain letters.
